scope: Read-only public help and served JavaScript inspection. No account creation, private browser storage inspection, or end-to-end recovery test.

findings: hx is cashu-nft-keys-v1; ia reads its JSON map.
dt derives public identity from the input private key and stores that same private-key string in the map.
MK reads the active private key from the map and reconstructs the session.
Po derives an AES-256-GCM key via HKDF-SHA-256 from the profile secret and mint keyset.
Encrypted credential records are stored in IndexedDB with per-record nonce and authenticated context.
saveAndExecute stores encrypted operation material locally and posts encrypted backup before execution.
recover decrypts returned card and operation backups using the derived key.

inference: Credential ciphertext is protected without the profile secret. Since the same-origin browser stores that secret without a password wrapper, obtaining the relevant browser storage can enable decryption; this is not equivalent to password-protected local key storage.
limits: Public client inspection does not establish server-side storage behavior or constitute an independent security audit.
Source may change after the observed asset hashes.
Active malicious site JavaScript can access secrets available to the app; an optional vault password primarily adds protection while locked.
